title: Ecology
short: The broad science of relationships among organisms and their environments—from individual responses and population change to communities, food webs, nutrients, and whole ecosystems.
bigPicture: Ecology asks how living systems work. Its subject can be a bacterial population, a plant community, a predator–prey relationship, a watershed, or the movement of energy and nutrients through an ecosystem. Ecologists build explanations from observation, experiments, long-term monitoring, and models. Their findings support conservation and natural-resource decisions, but the field itself is broader than wildlife and broader than management.

distinction.title: Ecology and Wildlife Ecology & Management
distinction.summary: The fields share population biology, field sampling, statistics, and spatial analysis. What they centre on, and what they produce, are different.

items.label: Ecology
items.description: Examines relationships across living systems. A project might center on microbes, plants, animals, species interactions, nutrient cycles, disturbance, or ecosystem function. Typical products include scientific explanations, models, monitoring results, and environmental assessments.

items.label: Wildlife Ecology & Management
items.description: Centers on free-ranging wild animals, their populations, and the habitats and people affecting them. Typical products include population estimates, species and habitat plans, harvest or protection recommendations, permits, and evaluated management actions.

terms.definition: A group of individuals of one species in a defined area, treated as a unit for study and management.
All the interacting species present in an area.
A community together with its physical environment, studied as a system of energy and material flows.
An organism's position in the food chain — producer, herbivore, predator — used to describe energy flow.
The population size an environment can sustain over time given available resources.
Repeated standardized measurement over many years, which is what makes it possible to distinguish a real trend from normal variation.

focus.title: Relationships across levels of life
focus.description: How individual organisms respond to conditions, how populations change, how species interact, and how those processes combine into communities and ecosystems.

focus.title: Ecosystems and energy flow
focus.description: How energy and matter move through systems, and how disturbance, nutrients, and climate shape what those systems can support.

focus.title: Field measurement and monitoring
focus.description: Designing sampling schemes, running surveys, and building long-term datasets, since most ecological claims depend on how the data were collected.

focus.title: Applied and environmental ecology
focus.description: Using ecological science in restoration, land management, environmental assessment, and policy, which is where a large share of the jobs are.
focus.source: Ecological Society of America (ESA): Certified Ecologist program

questions.question: What determines where a species can live and how many there are?
questions.approach: By combining occurrence surveys with environmental measurements, then modeling which conditions predict presence and testing predictions in new areas.

questions.question: How do species interactions structure a community?
questions.approach: Through removal or exclusion experiments, long-term observation, and comparison across sites where interacting species are present or absent.

questions.question: How does energy or matter move through this system?
questions.approach: By measuring inputs, outputs, and standing stocks, using isotopes and flux measurements to trace pathways instead of assuming them.

questions.question: How will this system respond to disturbance or environmental change?
questions.approach: By studying past disturbances, running manipulations where possible, and building models that project forward with stated uncertainty.

questions.question: Is what we are seeing a real trend or normal variation?
questions.approach: By analyzing long-term monitoring data with enough years to distinguish signal from noise, which is why long-running datasets are so valuable.

questions.question: Did the restoration or management action work?
questions.approach: By defining success measures before acting, monitoring treated and untreated areas, and continuing long enough for slow responses to appear.

responsibilities: Design and carry out field sampling, surveys, and monitoring.
Analyze ecological data and model system behavior.
Write technical reports, assessments, and peer-reviewed papers.
Advise on management, restoration, or regulatory decisions.
knowledgeSkills: Field sampling design and identification skills
geographic information systems (GIS) and spatial analysis

variations.label: Scale and subject
variations.description: Ecological work moves among organisms, populations, communities, and ecosystems. Plants, animals, microbes, soils, water, climate, and disturbance can all be central parts of the same investigation.

variations.label: There is a credential
variations.description: the Ecological Society of America (ESA) runs a professional certification program with a Certified Ecologist designation, assessed on education and experience and backed by a code of ethics. It is well known in consulting and agency work.
variations.source: Ecological Society of America (ESA): Certified Ecologist program

variations.label: Basic versus applied
variations.description: Research ecology and applied ecology in consulting, restoration, or agencies use the same science but differ in pace, output, and who the client is.

variations.label: Quantitative demand
variations.description: Ecology is a statistically heavy field, and comfort with data analysis increasingly separates competitive candidates from the rest.

realities: Statistical and data skills increasingly separate competitive candidates from the rest — and they are buildable as an undergraduate, deliberately.
Early field positions are commonly seasonal and modestly paid. Stacking several is a normal way in.
Expect coursework on plants, soils, and water. Animals are one part of the subject.
A good deal of applied ecology is report writing and regulatory compliance.
careers: M.S. / Ph.D. in wildlife ecology / conservation
